Air conditioning started as a fix for a printing press. In 1902, in Brooklyn, humid air warped the paper and the colours of a magazine never lined up.

Willis Carrier, an engineer aged 25, set one target: humidity. He ran chilled coils and fans through the plant and held it at 55 percent all year, 21 degrees in winter and 27 in summer. His drawings are dated 17 July 1902, the patent was granted in 1906, and by 1915 he had his own company.

Today 88 percent of United States homes have air conditioning, and the method is still his.
